title: Family care operates as distributed infrastructure with uneven private costs
source_unit: Deliberately non-pooled comparison of GAO kinship-family and assisted-living reviews, Federal Reserve SHED, Census SIPP, and BLS ATUS
geography: United States; national descriptive frames with selected-community and source-specific limits

kinship_to_foster_comparison.unit: kinship children outside foster care per child in foster care, approximate reported ratio

observations.method: GAO national descriptive Census/HHS frame plus selected community visits and caregiver interviews.
observations.uncertainty: Kinship-family definitions and foster-care status are not equivalent need measures; selected qualitative communities are not nationally representative.
observations.subgroup: Children raised by relatives or close family friends because parents cannot care for them.
observations.counterinterpretation: Kinship living can preserve relationships and continuity and is not itself evidence of hardship or inadequate care.

denominator.unit: valid person-record/month records in the child-care-use universe for selected paid-care measures; conditional measures have separate denominators

observations.method: Official SIPP universe and Fay-BRR records as preserved in the existing childcare work-adaptation record.
observations.uncertainty: Measures use different reference periods and conditional universes; time-loss estimates are less precise and do not identify a dated provider event or causal work loss.
observations.subgroup: Households with one or more members under 18 and relevant childcare/work fields.
observations.counterinterpretation: Paid-care use and work prevention can reflect employment, preference, resources, provider availability, or care need.

denominator.unit: source-specific survey and diary denominators; not pooled

regular_unpaid_adult_care.unit: percent of adults in 2025 SHED, source-reported

atus_2024_eldercare_minutes_difference.unit: provider minus nonprovider primary-activity minutes per diary day in standardized cells

atus_2024_paid_work_minutes_difference.unit: provider minus nonprovider paid-work minutes per diary day in standardized cells

observations.method: Separate published SHED care/work estimates and ATUS standardized diary contrasts.
observations.uncertainty: Cross-sectional and annual samples do not identify care onset, intensity, recipient outcomes, employer response, or causality; the measures are not pooled.
observations.subgroup: Adults reporting regular unpaid care and ATUS eldercare-roster providers versus comparison respondents.
observations.counterinterpretation: Care can be meaningful and reciprocal; time differences may reflect health, family support, distance, occupation, or selection.

denominator.unit: state Medicaid programs covering assisted-living services as of March 2025

observations.method: GAO review of assisted-living spending identification and state Medicaid coverage.
observations.uncertainty: Spending is likely undercounted because settings are not uniformly identified; coverage does not establish slots, affordability, quality, or receipt.
observations.subgroup: State Medicaid programs and assisted-living services, not individual residents.
observations.counterinterpretation: Public coverage and spending can coexist with room/board costs, waiting, family substitution, and uneven local capacity.

related_sources.claim: Kinship family scale, formal-status split, and caregiver/community boundaries.
Assisted-living spending and state coverage architecture.
SHED care, living arrangement, and work-adaptation evidence.
Existing SIPP, SHED, ATUS, and NHTS care/time/material comparison.

boundary: This is a deliberately non-pooled family-care capacity synthesis. It supports distributed care capacity and uneven private-cost mechanisms across US evidence surfaces, but does not estimate a common care burden, causal intervention effect, verified support receipt, recovery, trust, political action, or household-to-state consequence. A dated same-family care episode with alternatives and follow-up remains open.
